title: IndiGo Website Outage Blocks Flight Bookings and Check-Ins Across India
excerpt: India's largest airline by market share experienced a website malfunction that prevented customers from booking tickets, with third-party platforms also reporting disruptions.
body:
• IndiGo's website displayed "no data available" errors on Wednesday, preventing customers from booking flights or completing online check-ins.
  • The outage affected users across multiple Indian cities, with third-party travel booking platforms also reporting disruptions linked to IndiGo's systems.
  • IndiGo controls more than 65% of India's domestic aviation market, meaning the outage had outsized impact on travelers across the country.
  • The airline faced similar scrutiny in December after poor pilot roster planning forced it to cancel around 4,500 flights.

Booking System Goes Dark

IndiGo, India's largest airline, experienced a website outage on Wednesday that prevented customers from booking tickets and completing online check-ins. The airline's website displayed a "no data available" message when users searched for flights, according to Reuters, which confirmed the issue through journalists in at least three Indian cities.

The disruption extended beyond IndiGo's own platform. At least one third-party travel booking website displayed a message stating that "the airline systems are currently experiencing a technical problem," suggesting the issue was rooted in IndiGo's backend systems rather than its website front end alone.

"The airline's website displayed a "no data available" message when users searched for flights, according to Reuters, which confirmed the issue through journalists in at least three Indian cities."

Passengers Turn to Social Media

Travelers took to X (formerly Twitter) to report their inability to book flights or complete check-in procedures. The complaints ranged from failed ticket purchases to disrupted online check-in flows — a particular concern for passengers with imminent departures who rely on digital boarding passes.

IndiGo, which operates more than 2,000 daily flights including international routes, did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the cause of the outage or an estimated time for restoration.

A Pattern of Operational Disruptions

The outage comes at a sensitive time for IndiGo's reputation. In December, the airline came under sharp scrutiny from India's aviation regulator after poor pilot roster planning forced it to cancel approximately 4,500 flights over a matter of days, stranding tens of thousands of passengers and creating chaotic scenes at airports across the country.

The Directorate General of Civil Aviation ordered an urgent investigation and demanded IndiGo submit a comprehensive roadmap for crew recruitment, training, and roster restructuring. The Civil Aviation Minister at the time expressed "clear displeasure" at IndiGo's handling of the crisis.

The airline has also weathered multiple technology-related disruptions over the past two years, including issues linked to the global CrowdStrike outage and an Airbus software advisory that affected its A320 fleet.

Market Dominance Magnifies Impact

IndiGo's market share — more than 65% of India's domestic aviation traffic — means any system failure at the airline has an outsized ripple effect. The carrier operates a vast network connecting metro hubs, tier-2 cities, and a growing number of international destinations. When its booking systems go down, a majority of Indian domestic air travelers are directly affected.

The airline's parent company, InterGlobe Aviation, trades on India's National Stock Exchange under the ticker INGL.

What Travelers Should Know

Passengers with upcoming IndiGo flights should check flight status directly through the airline's app or by calling IndiGo's customer service line. Those unable to complete online check-in should arrive at the airport early, as manual check-in at counters may be required. For new bookings, travelers may want to try third-party platforms or wait until IndiGo confirms its systems are fully restored.
